questions.question: A network administrator configured an EtherChannel link with three interfaces between two switches. What is the result if one of the three interfaces is down?
questions.answer: The remaining two interfaces continue to load balance traffic.
choices: b. The remaining two interfaces become separate links between the two switches.
c. The remaining two interfaces continue to load balance traffic.
d. One interface becomes an active link for data traffic and the other becomes a backup link.

questions.question: A network administrator is analyzing the features that are supported by different first-hop router redundancy protocols. Which statement describes a feature that is associated with HSRP?
questions.answer: HSRP uses active and standby routers.
choices: a. It allows load balancing between a group of redundant routers.
c. HSRP uses active and standby routers.
d. It uses ICMP messages in order to assign the default gateway to hosts.

questions.question: A network administrator is analyzing the features that are supported by different first-hop router redundancy protocols. Which statement is a feature that is associated with GLBP?
questions.answer: GLBP allows load balancing between routers.
choices: a. It uses a virtual router master.
c. It works together with VRRP.
d. GLBP allows load balancing between routers.

After the election of the root bridge has been completed, how will switches find the best paths to the root bridge?
questions.answer: Each switch will analyze the sum of all port costs to reach the root and use the path with the lowest cost.
choices: a. Each switch will analyze the BID of all neighbors to reach the root and use the path through the lowest BID neighbors.
b. Each switch will analyze the sum of all port costs to reach the root and use the path with the lowest cost.
c. Each switch will analyze the sum of the hops to reach the root and use the path with the fewest hops.
d. Each switch will analyze the port states of all neighbors and use the designated ports to forward traffic to the root.

questions.question: What is an accurate description of redundancy?
questions.answer: designing a network to use multiple paths between switches to ensure there is no single point of failure
